notes: Use-case summary: replace legacy keyword search for compliance requests and subpoenas. Primary flow: ingestion -> embeddings -> ANN search -> reranking -> result set for attorneys.
Indexing scale: customer expects initial production index ~3M-5M documents, plan to grow to ~20M within 12 months. Chunking strategy yields ~3-4x embeddings relative to doc count.

Latency & throughput: target p95 response < 300ms for reranked top-10 on typical queries; peak throughput 120 qps during discovery events. Cost sensitivity: want cost-per-query under $0.05 for average search, lower for high-volume batch reprocessing.
Model preferences: prefer open models for token-cost control; evaluating quantized variants. Want deterministic reranker (repeatable scoring) and ability to pin model versions for auditability.
Routing & fallbacks: must be able to failover to a cold-hosted endpoint in a different region if on-prem capacity is exhausted. Prefer unified API surface across modes.

Security/compliance: strict data residency (US-only for regulated clients), SSO (SAML/SCIM), immutable audit logs with tamper-evident storage, retention zones up to 7 years, KMS w/ customer CMKs and HSM-backed key wrapping.

POC notes: initial embedding pipeline used Faiss/IVF on a sample corpus. Observed vector store build time ~3 hours for 200k embeddings on baseline instance; need Redwood's optimize recommendations for bulk indexing.
Quotes: "We need forensics-grade audit trails — every query, model version, and rerank score must be reproducible for e-discovery." (Head of Compliance)
Security ask: provide architecture diagram for Redwood Private VPC, details on audit log retention and immutability, KMS integration instructions, and SOC2 artifact references.
Operational asks: can Redwood provide automated reindexing jobs with incremental embedding updates and a suggested autoscaling policy for peak e-discovery windows?
Risks: cross-border transfer restrictions for a subset of clients (EU-origin data) — need clear residency and TOS language; legal is cautious about any vendor-side caching beyond ephemeral KV cache.

Decision drivers: clear cost-per-query model, proof that reranking at 20M scale meets latency SLOs, lock-step security assurances (SOC2/ISO) and support for long-term retention + WORM-like audit logging.
